title: Morning Headlines
intro: A day of escalating conflict and consequential decisions: the U.S.-Iran war intensifies, Washington opens a fresh trade front against Brazil, China's economy shows new cracks, Britain's next prime minister is effectively decided, and SpaceX targets its first payload-carrying Starship flight.

items.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Again as Tehran Threatens to 'Crush' Regional Infrastructure
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera / CNN
items.summary: U.S. forces carried out another wave of strikes on Iranian military sites on July 16, targeting coastal surveillance and missile facilities while a naval blockade of Iranian ports remained in force. Iran's military warned it would crush 'all infrastructure in the region' if the U.S. attacks civilian sites, raising fears of a wider regional war as ceasefire talks remain stalled.

items.title: U.S. Hits Brazil with 25% Tariffs Over 'Unfair Trade Practices'
items.subtitle: CNBC / CNN Business
items.summary: The Trump administration announced sweeping 25% tariffs on most Brazilian imports, effective July 22, following a yearlong USTR investigation into discriminatory barriers and lax anti-corruption enforcement — opening a significant new front in U.S. trade policy in Latin America. Brazil condemned the move, and a separate forced-labor probe could add another 12.5% on top.

items.title: China's Economy Posts Slowest Quarterly Growth Since 2022
items.subtitle: CNBC / China National Bureau of Statistics
items.summary: China's GDP grew 4.7% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, but Q2 slipped to just 4.3% — the weakest reading since 2022 — as sluggish consumer spending and business investment offset strong exports driven partly by the global AI boom. The figure falls within Beijing's 4.5–5% annual target but underscores persistent structural headwinds facing the world's second-largest economy.

items.title: Andy Burnham Set to Become UK Prime Minister After Nomination Deadline Passes
items.subtitle: PBS NewsHour / Al Jazeera
items.summary: Labour Party leadership nominations closed today with Andy Burnham mathematically certain to be the only candidate, meaning he will be formally announced as Britain's next prime minister on July 17 — ending a leadership crisis triggered by Keir Starmer's resignation in June. Burnham's near-certain appointment will make him the UK's seventh prime minister in ten years.

items.title: SpaceX Targets Starship Flight 13 — First Mission to Carry Starlink Satellites
items.subtitle: Space.com / SpaceX
items.summary: SpaceX is targeting a July 16 evening launch for Starship's 13th test flight, the first to carry a commercial payload — 20 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites — while also attempting a Raptor engine relight in orbit and a Super Heavy booster catch. Success would mark the transition of the world's most powerful rocket from test vehicle to operational launcher.
